rv.q: This is frequently a fun show with a cute framing device of a small boy on-stage in awe of his heroes.
It isn't original and it certainly isn't politically correct but it's still a glittering, occasionally gobsmacking night out.
So Impossible is not a brave new dawn for British magic.

It’s a highly entertaining show, but also somewhat retro in its suggestion that the chief function of women is to be bundled into cabinets and bisected, made to disappear or invisibly transported from one side of the stage to the other.
Impossible cannot reinvent the genre and knows it. It can only put new spins on old tricks.

It has been over a hundred years since the famous magician Henry Houdini performed one of his great escape acts in front of over 4000 people at London’s Hippodrome. This summer the production of Impossible at the Noel Coward Theatre brings back magic to the capital with its attempt to give It a fresh and a contemporary twist.
Impossible is not a brave new dawn for British magic. Yet it’s too full of skill to resist for long.

cn.t: A spectacular but uneven magic show packs in impressive illusions and death-defying stunts, though critics note its dated gender politics, cheesy tone, and inconsistent pacing undercut the occasional gobsmacking moments.
